caption: Twenty-five years of night shifts and there's never once been a month with room for retirement savings. Is 55 too late, or does everyone feel that way?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R19 800
p/m salary
Living in Komani (Queenstown)
slides.body:
Male, 55
Divorced, kids grown and moved out
Job: Night security supervisor, retail complex
Net salary: R19 800 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: Downsized twice since the divorce. This is about as small as it gets before it's not worth it.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Cooking for one now, still buy in bulk out of habit
slides.body: Habits from a bigger household don't disappear just because the household did.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi to the complex for night shift, six nights a week
slides.body: There's no late-night alternative that's cheaper or safer.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Hospital plan only, no day-to-day cover
slides.body: At 55 I know exactly what this doesn't cover, and I've made peace with hoping I don't need it.

slides.title: Funeral policy
slides.includes: Covers me and my two kids
slides.body: The one policy I've never missed a premium on, not even the year everything else was late.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Cellphone & data, stokvel, money to my daughter and grandchild when I can, church, a uniform replacement now and then
slides.body: There's no line here for retirement. Twenty-five years of night shifts and I've never once had a spare amount to start one.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R19 800. Enough to get through the month. Not enough, at 55, to feel like there's a plan underneath it.

slides.title: I finally looked at the whole picture, not just this month
slides.body:
I uploaded my statements to Beyond Horizon to see the pattern, not just one payslip. Twenty-five years in, there was never a month with room for retirement savings — now at least I can see it clearly instead of guessing.

No bank login needed.
